pairs.registryProposal: passive-signal-ingestion says a watch attempt ends in one of three verdicts but does not say where the verdict is stored when the watcher is a stateless poll function. Personas' shape — a poll returning Result<Vec<Event>> plus a subscription row — makes 'could-not-observe' need a durable column on the subscription AND a rule that the freshness watermark must not advance on a failed pass. The second half (a failed observation must not advance the since-cursor) is a real, separable claim the technique does not currently make, and it is what turns a transient blindness into permanent data loss.

techniques.evidence: src/features/onboarding/components/GuidedTour.tsx:204-208 anchors every step by `highlightTestId`, i.e. the identifiers the test suite already keeps honest, maintained on the elements themselves; src/stores/slices/system/tourSlice.ts:1709-1719 validates identifier syntax at the single setter door and refuses a malformed id; src/stores/slices/system/__tests__/tourAnchors.test.ts is the generated, source-derived manifest gate that fails at commit time on a vanished anchor; and geometry is a live derivation with re-resolution rather than a cached rect (src/hooks/utility/interaction/useTrackedElementRect.ts:36-53).

src/features/onboarding/components/useTourNarration.ts:15-16 states and enforces that narration never advances or blocks a step; :71 makes it inert when no voice is configured, :116/:141 keep synthesis errors as a control status rather than a tour error, and :148-179 stop playback on step change, mute and unmount, with mute persisted as a preference rather than a per-step toggle.

src/stores/slices/system/tourSlice.ts:1401-1402 rebuilds the slice against a hardcoded default tour, so the active-tour half of the resume pair is never persisted; and :1452 stores the cursor as `currentStepIndex`, position-based identity the technique explicitly refuses (inserting a step mid-tour resumes the wrong one), even though completion is correctly keyed by step id at :1607. The rest is strong: per-tour progress written on every transition (:1446-1457), a versioned payload (:1130), completion/dismissed as separate recorded outcomes, an out-of-range clamp on hydrate (:1409), a storage probe that surfaces unavailable persistence once with a Sentry breadcrumb instead of silently resetting (:1167-1199), and skip-on-the-last-step refusing to force-mark the tour complete (:1570-1584).

src/stores/slices/system/tourSlice.ts:1388,1471 provide exactly one global degradation flag (`tourHighlightMissing`, set at src/features/onboarding/components/TourSpotlight.tsx:31-33) and every step re-centers with a 'not on screen yet' note — a single global policy where the technique requires skip-or-recenter declared per step, because only the author knows whether the step survives its anchor's absence. The degradation also leaves no trace: nothing records which tour, step, anchor and policy fired, so a step whose anchor rots is invisible in completion accounting even though the repo already ships Sentry. Conformant on the invariant that matters most — the overlay is pointer-events-none, the panel controls and exit never depend on resolution, and patience is bounded at 4×500ms (src/hooks/utility/interaction/useTrackedElementRect.ts:40-41).

The completion half is exemplary and worth keeping: TourPanelBody.tsx:191-213 labels the forward control 'Skip' (de-emphasized) on an incomplete step and 'Continue' only once the step is genuinely done, so no user can advance believing they performed an action they did not; completion fires from real product state (GuidedTour.tsx:187,197 → tourSlice.ts:1613-1621) and nothing auto-advances on a timer.

src/features/onboarding/components/GuidedTour.tsx:462 (and TourNarrativeDeck.tsx:86-90, which hand-coordinates 9998 vs 9999 in a comment) mint the tour's own layer numbers; the product has no layering authority to register into — z-values are ad hoc per feature (z-50 in CrossProjectMetadataModal.tsx, z-[120] in StudioTabBar.tsx, z-[60] in StudioAttention.tsx) — so the tour's rank against dialogs and alerts is unstated and unprovable. Escape is also reinterpreted: GuidedTour.tsx:255 minimizes instead of leaving, while the tour is dimming the product behind it. Conformant on conduct at collision: :260 yields the screen entirely to the onboarding modal and resumes at the same step, and the tour runs no focus trap.

pairs.subject: design-tokens
pairs.evidence: src/styles/globals.css:832 applies the brightness axis as `filter: brightness()` on <html> — the whole-surface pixel filter the standard names as a trap — so every contrast number the product computes (CustomThemeCreator.tsx:33) describes declarations that never reach the screen, and the compensation list it forces (globals.css:852-857) is already growing.

techniques.evidence: src/styles/globals.css:831-833 implements brightness (and dim, :838-840) as a pixel filter over the rendered output instead of rebinding the surface ramp, which escapes the token layer on both teeth the technique names: gates read values the screen never shows, and distinct tints are clamped — visible in the counter-measures it requires, `brightness-lock` (:847-850), a hardcoded compensated-class list (:852-857) and a TS list of exempt tokens re-read through getComputedStyle (src/stores/themeStore.ts:219-241). The axes are also not disjoint: both density and text-scale rebind the same `.typo-body` overrides (globals.css:811-814, 'Mirrors the data-text-scale typo overrides'), so source order decides and the settings screen can lie. And only theme + text-scale are stamped before first paint (public/theme-init.js) — density, brightness, dim, contrast and motion are applied after rehydrate (src/stores/themeStore.ts:379-383), so a compact, dimmed user gets a flash of the defaults at every launch. Conformant on the core move for density and text scale: each is one root attribute driving token overrides (themeStore.ts:167,211), and components never learn the axis exists.

There is no follow-the-platform state: no `prefers-color-scheme` or matchMedia read exists anywhere in src/stores/themeStore.ts or public/theme-init.js, and the default is a hardcoded `dark-midnight` (themeStore.ts:286) with `class="dark"` baked into index.html — so the model is two-state where the standard requires three, and the most common state (never opened the setting) is the untested one. Custom themes also ship without passing a contrast gate: src/features/settings/sub_appearance/components/CustomThemeCreator.tsx:266 gates Save only on a non-empty label while :33-35 renders the WCAG ratios as an advisory readout, moving the accessibility floor into the user's hands. Conformant on rebinding at a scope root (themeStore.ts:149-151), on a retired-theme migration that cannot strand a user (:369-372), and — notably well — on derived themes naming their derivation: the seed config is what is stored and `deriveCustomThemeVars` re-runs it on every rehydrate (:373-374), so adding a role does not orphan the theme.

eslint.config.js:96-105 sets every token rule the repo wrote to `warn` and `custom/no-raw-spacing-classes` to `off` — the advisory neutering the technique names as the most common way this gate dies; not one raw-value rule can fail a build, so the floor is persuasion. The in-context consequence is visible immediately: AppearanceThemingSection.tsx:53 inlines a raw `minmax(140px, 1fr)` grid track and AppearanceBrightnessSettings.tsx:49 sizes with raw `w-5 h-5`, neither of which any gate can stop. The rule family itself is unusually complete (no-raw-text/spacing/shadow/radius-classes, no-low-contrast-text-classes, no-direct-white-colors) — only the severity is missing.

AppearanceThemingSection.tsx:34 (`text-violet-400`), AppearanceBrightnessSettings.tsx:49 (`text-amber-400`) and AppearanceDensitySettings.tsx:123 consume Tailwind palette primitives directly at call sites while the product does define semantic roles for exactly this (`--brand-violet`, `--status-*`, enumerated at src/stores/themeStore.ts:219-231) — the skipped-layer anti-pattern, and a fixed hex that no theme can rebind. Conformant on typography, which is recipe-shaped throughout (`typo-body`, `typo-caption`, `typo-heading`) rather than loose size/weight ingredients, and on radius roles (`rounded-modal`, `rounded-card`, `rounded-interactive`).

src/stores/themeStore.ts:219-231 hand-maintains a TypeScript list of CSS custom-property names and reads them back with getComputedStyle at :239-241, guarded by `if (current)` — so renaming or removing a token in the stylesheet makes it silently lose its brightness immunity with no gate and no error. The brightness ladder is duplicated too: the authored values live in themeStore.ts:34-45 and are restated in a globals.css comment (:818-819), with the `--app-brightness: 1.25` default (globals.css:826) a third copy of `brightness: 'low'` (themeStore.ts:289) — hand-sync with a comment, which the technique classifies as not a strategy.

src/stores/themeStore.ts:198-204 makes reduced motion a token-layer decision — one `data-motion="reduce"` attribute at the scope root that CSS honors globally (relied on at src/features/onboarding/components/TourSpotlight.tsx:50-54) — backed by a dedicated lint rule, eslint-rules/enforce-reduced-motion-fallback.cjs. The duration/easing ladders themselves are defined outside this context and were not evaluated here.

pairs.registryProposal: density-and-scale-axes warns that a whole-surface pixel filter escapes the token layer. This repo is a measured field case worth citing in the application layer: the filter forced a compensation vocabulary — an exempt-token list, a `brightness-lock` utility, and a hardcoded list of Tailwind class prefixes to counter-filter (globals.css:852-857) — which is the exact 'growing dialect' signature the enforcement technique predicts, arriving through the axis rather than through a deadline commit. The trap's second tooth also has a sharper form than the technique states: the product's own contrast instrument (CustomThemeCreator.tsx:33) measures the pre-filter declarations, so the filter does not merely evade an external gate, it invalidates the one the product shows its users.

pairs.subject: client-state
pairs.evidence: src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/sceneStore.ts:109-118 dispatches family loads with no latest-wins token and no in-flight dedup, so a slow first load landing after a newer one silently repaints the canvas with superseded data — and src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/layoutStore.ts:216 re-stamps any future-version document as the current version, destroying fields a newer build wrote.

techniques.evidence: src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/sceneStore.ts:120-133 runs a per-project invalidation with no per-entity status: its failure is swallowed with a comment, leaving no state anywhere, so that one project's scan cells keep rendering as current — the keyed-machine rule (one machine per independently-running operation instance) is unmet exactly where the operations became per-entity. Also, loadScans/loadMeta set `loading` on every refresh (:110,:99) even when data is held, conflating loading with the stale-with-data case the same file otherwise models. The core is strong and tested: FamilyStatus is one enumerated set per family (:34-38), and `failStatus` (:74-76) is the single shared transition-on-failure function the technique asks for, sending loaded/stale→stale and idle/loading→failed, asserted at __tests__/sceneStore.test.ts:49-58.

src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/sceneStore.ts contains no request token, dedup registry or abort anywhere (grep: reqId/seq/token/inFlight/dedup/abort → none); loadScans (:109), loadMeta (:98) and loadSentry (:135) all write their response into the slot unconditionally, so two concurrent loads of the same family resolve last-writer-wins by arrival order. The throttles at :75,:80 bound frequency but are not guards — `force: true` bypasses them into exactly the racing case. The repo already owns the right primitive (`createLatestWins`, used at src/features/teams/sub_teamMemory/components/diff/RunDiffView.tsx:54), so this is an unused utility rather than a missing one.

src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/layoutStore.ts:216 unconditionally writes `version: LAYOUT_DOC_VERSION` onto whatever it parsed, so a v3 document written by a newer build is silently downgraded to v2 and re-saved — the future-payload direction the technique requires be handled deliberately (preserve-and-default), and the same file gets it right one level down for panel specs (:191, membership test against SUPPORTED_PANEL_SPEC_VERSIONS, unknown versions dropped rather than coerced). Everything else is exemplary and tested: the durable app DB is the authority with localStorage demoted to a fallback (__tests__/layoutStore.test.ts:155-168), the version lives inside the payload under a stable key (:39-43, 'the version FIELD is what moves'), the v1→v2 author backfill is a real migration step (:172-183), legacy localStorage keys are imported once and written through (test :100-118), and a corrupt document falls back to empty without throwing (test :93-98).

src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/layoutStore.ts:103 holds the debounce timer (and the in-memory doc and listener set) at module scope with no generation token and no globalThis anchor — and this is the case the technique says is real rather than benign, because a superseded copy's pending timer performs a write observable outside the process: after an HMR re-evaluation the old module flushes its stale doc to the shared `mastermind.layout.v1` row and reverts canvas edits the new copy already hydrated. The test-reset hatch half is present and exercised (`__resetLayoutStoreForTests`, __tests__/persistence.test.ts:7,17 and layoutStore.test.ts:60,130).

src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/sceneStore.ts:7-9 states and implements the discipline — surgical event-driven invalidation instead of a timer — with `invalidateScans(projectId)` (:120-133) patching one project's entry rather than dropping the family, and the remote families keeping only a demoted refresh floor (MONITOR_MIN_INTERVAL :75, LLM_SPEND_MIN_INTERVAL :80) as a backstop.

src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/layoutStore.ts:205-222 guards every field independently against its own default, so one corrupt key cannot reset the whole canvas; :185-196 validates panel specs by membership in an enumerable closed set (`SUPPORTED_PANEL_SPEC_VERSIONS.has(...)`) — a run-time test on the value, not a type assertion; and __tests__/persistence.test.ts:51-59 pins that getters hand out fresh containers so a caller cannot mutate the store through a read.

src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/sceneStore.ts:84-133 is one slice per domain of change whose every mutation goes through an operation it defines (loadX / invalidateScans / retryFailed), and the derived view is computed at read time rather than stored — `deriveScene` is a pure function over the families, covered at __tests__/deriveScene.*.test.ts. The repo also enforces the subscription half with a dedicated lint rule (eslint-rules/no-whole-store-subscription.cjs).

The canvas layout's authority is local: src/features/teams/sub_mastermind/lib/layoutStore.ts writes memory first and debounces through to the app's own DB, with no remote authority that can disagree and nothing to reconcile or revert; the precondition (painting a change before an authority has agreed to it) does not hold.

The families this context caches are read from the local application database (dev projects, scans, goals, runner tasks) rather than fetched on behalf of a switchable remote identity, so an account flip cannot make an entry illegitimate here. Noted for the registry rather than as a deviation of this pair: src/stores/authStore.ts:79-93 clears only auth fields and the crypto cache on logout, evicting no caches at all — worth judging in whichever context owns auth.

No dependency manifest, derived init order or acyclicity assertion was found (grep for storeGraph/topolog/acyclic across src/stores and src/lib returned nothing relevant), but I did not measure the real edge count or look for a cycle among the module stores this context uses (sceneStore, layoutStore, focusStore, canvasActionStore), so I cannot say whether the technique's precondition — a graph that outgrew one author's memory — holds here.

pairs.registryProposal: This context is a test directory, and it surfaced something the subject does not currently say: several of these techniques are testable as behaviours, and the repo proves it — the shared failure-transition function is pinned at __tests__/sceneStore.test.ts:49-58, the restart round-trip and the IPC-unavailable fallback at __tests__/layoutStore.test.ts:120-168, and the reset hatch is exercised in every beforeEach. status-fsms, persistence-and-migration and singleton-lifecycle would each be stronger with a named verification shape (the fixtures that prove them), the way project-identity-and-joins already carries its three tests.

pairs.subject: diff-comparison
pairs.evidence: src/features/teams/sub_teamMemory/libs/memoryDiff.ts:50-55 aligns two runs by memory id, but `get_by_run` selects `WHERE run_id = ?1` (src-tauri/db/src/repos/resources/team_memories.rs:99), so the two sets are disjoint by construction — every run diff reports 100% of B as 'new learnings' and 100% of A as 'no longer present'.

techniques.evidence: src/features/teams/sub_teamMemory/libs/memoryDiff.ts:48 documents the alignment ('matching is by memory ID -- memories created in different runs have different IDs') while :18-21 labels the output `added` = 'new learnings' and `removed` = 'no longer present'; because a memory row carries exactly one run_id, no element of run A can ever match an element of run B, so the vocabulary is strictly stronger than the alignment supports and the panel asserts knowledge creation and loss that never happened. src/features/teams/sub_teamMemory/libs/useRunDiffSummaries.ts:82-87 carries the same defect into the timeline markers, where added always equals current.length and removed always equals prev.length.
